Ben: Hi Chloe! Do you want to see the new Space Cats film on Saturday?
Chloe: Yes! But not in the morning. I've got a swimming lesson until twelve.
Ben: OK. There's a show at two fifteen and one at five thirty.
Chloe: Let's go to the earlier one. My mum wants me home for dinner.

Chloe: Great, I've got my card. Shall we get popcorn?
Ben: It's really expensive there. I'll bring some snacks from home.
Chloe: Good idea. Where shall we meet?
Ben: In front of the cinema, ten minutes before the start.
Chloe: Perfect. See you on Saturday!

title: The eco project
situation_ru: Нина и Алекс выбирают идею для школьного эко-проекта.
situation_en: Nina and Alex are choosing an idea for their school eco project.
script:
Nina: So, we need an idea for the eco project by Friday. Any thoughts?
Alex: What about a poster about recycling?
Nina: Hmm, everyone does posters. Mr Brown said he wants something original.
Alex: OK, how about a clothes swap? People bring clothes they don't wear any more and swap them with other people.
Nina: Oh, I like that! My sister has a whole wardrobe of stuff she never wears.
Alex: We could do it in the school hall on a Saturday.
Nina: The hall's being used for the dance competition next month, though. What about the library?
Alex: Too small. Maybe the gym, after classes on a Wednesday?
Nina: Perfect. And we could charge fifty cents to come in and give the money to the animal shelter.
Alex: Great. I'll talk to Mr Brown tomorrow, and you can make the posters.
Nina: So we're doing posters after all!
Alex: Ha! Only to advertise it.

title: Study Hacks
situation_ru: Лео ведёт подкаст для школьников и рассказывает, как перестал откладывать уроки.
situation_en: Leo hosts a podcast for students. Today he talks about how he stopped putting things off.
script: Leo: Hi, and welcome back to Study Hacks, the podcast for students who'd rather be doing anything except studying. I'm Leo. [pause 1s] Today's topic is procrastination, or, in simple words, putting things off. I used to be the king of it. I'd sit down to do my homework, then check my phone just for a second, and suddenly it was midnight. [pause 1s] So what changed? Last year I tried something called the Pomodoro technique. You set a timer for twenty-five minutes and work without stopping. Then you take a five-minute break. After four of these, you have a longer break. It sounds too simple to work, but it really helped me. The secret is that twenty-five minutes doesn't feel scary. [pause 1s] My other tip: put your phone in another room. Not on your desk, not in your pocket. Another room. Next week I'll be talking about how to revise for exams without losing your mind. See you then!

questions.q: Who is the podcast for?
options: Young people looking for a job
questions.explain_ru: «for students who'd rather be doing anything except studying».

questions.q: What was Leo's problem in the past?
options: He studied until midnight every day
questions.explain_ru: Он постоянно откладывал уроки: «I used to be the king of it».

questions.q: How long is a short break in the Pomodoro technique?
Why does Leo think the technique works?
options: It's quite complicated, so you have to concentrate hard
His teacher made him use it

questions.explain_ru: «The secret is that twenty-five minutes doesn't feel scary».

title: Weekends at the shelter
situation_ru: Интервью на радио с Дэниелом, который по выходным помогает в приюте для животных.
situation_en: A radio host interviews Daniel, who volunteers at an animal shelter at weekends.
script:
Host: Today I'm talking to Daniel, who's sixteen and spends his weekends at an animal shelter. Daniel, how did it all start?
Daniel: Honestly, it was my mum's idea. She thought I was spending too much time on video games, so she signed me up without asking me. I was pretty annoyed at first.
Host: And now?
Daniel: Now I can't imagine my weekends without it. I've been going there for almost two years.
Host: What do you actually do there?
Daniel: Mostly I walk the dogs and clean the cages, which isn't very glamorous. But I also take photos of the animals for the shelter's website. Good photos really help animals find new homes faster.
Host: What's the hardest part?
Daniel: Saying goodbye, definitely. You get attached to them. But it's the best feeling when a dog you've looked after for months finally goes home with a family.
Host: Would you recommend volunteering to other teenagers?
Daniel: Absolutely. Just maybe ask them before you sign them up!

questions.q: How did Daniel start volunteering?
options: His school made him do it
questions.explain_ru: «it was my mum's idea… she signed me up».

questions.explain_ru: «Good photos really help animals find new homes faster».
